response.passage: In the bustling town of Ooty, local tea shop owner Mr. Sharma recently compared his monthly sales to understand his growth. In January, he sold 450 cups of masala chai to tourists. By February, after he introduced a special ginger blend, his sales jumped to 600 cups. Mr. Sharma explains that the increase happened because the cold weather attracted more visitors to his shop. Meanwhile, his competitor, Mrs. Iyer, who runs a bakery nearby, sold only 300 pastries in February. She believes her lower sales are due to her shop being located further from the main bus stand. Mr. Sharma notes that while his cup count is higher, comparing quantities requires looking at the total profit, not just the volume of items sold. He warns that just because his sales increased, it does not mean every shop in Ooty saw a rise in customers. He reminds his staff that 'volume' in business refers specifically to the total number of units sold, not the loudness of the customers inside.
response.summary: Mr. Sharma compares his tea shop's sales growth between January and February. He explains that cold weather boosted his sales, while Mrs. Iyer attributes her lower sales to her shop's location. The passage highlights that comparing business performance involves more than just counting units.
